subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should credential-named assignment values be exempted only when they match a strict code-reference grammar, or should autoreview retain root-based allowlisting for language-agnostic safety?
rationale: The same unquoted token shape can be a harmless JavaScript or TypeScript reference and a literal plain scalar in another reviewed format, so the accepted grammar changes the secret-exposure boundary.

options.title: Strict reference grammar
options.body: Accept exact identifiers and member-access expressions through narrowly bounded parsing while keeping literals, operators, calls, templates, and ambiguous plain scalars fail-closed.

options.title: Expand the root allowlist
options.body: Add common roots such as ctx and environment, reducing the reported failures while retaining name-dependent false positives.

options.title: Keep the current boundary
options.body: Retain current fail-closed behavior and document destructuring or renaming workarounds, accepting continued branch-review friction.

recommendation.title: Strict reference grammar
recommendation.body: Accept exact identifiers and member-access expressions through narrowly bounded parsing while keeping literals, operators, calls, templates, and ambiguous plain scalars fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work most directly defines the scanner’s current fail-closed and false-positive boundaries.
